title: Trauma Education and Training in US Graduate Counseling and Health Service Psychology Programs: A 26‐Year Scoping Review
abstract: ABSTRACT This PRISMA Scoping Review systematically mapped 42 peer‐reviewed articles on trauma education and training within US graduate counseling and health service psychology programs over a 26‐year period (1999–2024). We descriptively summarized publication characteristics and mapped findings concerning trauma education content and delivery, educator preparation and support, and programmatic structures and systemic initiatives. Most articles were published since 2019 and were conceptual rather than empirical. Coverage across the research questions was uneven. The literature focused primarily on trauma content, status of trauma education, and andragogy‐related content. Educator preparation and support received comparatively less attention, whereas programmatic structures and systemic initiatives were addressed in nearly half of the articles. Overall, the literature offered more guidance on what trauma education should include and how it might be organized than empirical evidence on its implementation, evaluation, and sustainment. Further research should evaluate these educational approaches and the support needed to implement them.
